case_name: State of Punjab v Buta Singh and Others
facts: On 4.7.1991 at about 8.00 PM A-2 (Hadayat) armed with a takua and A-4 (Suba) armed with kirpan went to the house of Sheela, the sister-in-law of complainant Malok and insisted her to open the door.
When the complainant who was said to be present inside the house, questioned them as to why they are troubling her sister-in-law and children these two persons tried to kill the complainant.

It is alleged that Buta raised a lalkara that they should not spare the complainant and so saying gave a takua blow from the reverse side on the chest of complainant (Malok) and the same was followed by A-3 by giving a dang blow on the right hand.
On alarm being raised by the complainant party, the accused ran away from the spot with their respective weapons.
petitioner_arguments: The trial court though has referred to the evidence in detail seems to have committed an error in not properly analysing the same with reference to the involvement and role of A-3 and A-4.

To this extent the consideration by the High Court and the appreciation of the evidence, in our view, appears to be reasonable and the conclusions arrived at to affirm the conviction of only A-1 and A-2 are found to be well merited.
court_reasoning: The trial court though has referred to the evidence in detail seems to have committed an error in not properly analysing the same with reference to the involvement and role of A-3 and A-4.

In our view, the consideration by the High Court and the appreciation of the evidence, in our view, appears to be reasonable and the conclusions arrived at to affirm the conviction of only A-1 and A-2 are found to be well merited.

As long as the conclusions arrived at by the High Court are found to be justified on an appreciation of the evidence on record in their proper perspective and which is not shown to be perverse or arbitrary, there is hardly any justification for this Court to interfere with the verdict of acquittal.
holding: The appeal fails and shall stand dismissed.
cases_cited: State of Punjab v Buta Singh
